Judgment :

1. Insurance Company/original opponent no.2 hereby challenges judgment and award passed by learned Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ahmednagar in MACP No.245 of 2015 thereby partly allowing the claim set up by present respondent nos.1 to 5, under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

2. In short, present respondent nos.1 to 5, who are original claimants and heirs of one Ganesh, set up claim petition alleging that on 18-04-2015, deceased was returning to his village as a pillion rider over Motorcycle bearing registration No. MH-16 AU-8799.

In the vicinity of Patharwadi Shivar, a Milk Tanker bearing registration No. MH-45-4989 coming from opposite direction, gave dash to the Motorcycle causing fatal injuries resulting into death of pillion rider.
That, crime was registered against Tanker driver.
On account of loss {3} FA 1363 OF 2017 of income and dependency, above compensation claim petition was instituted.
As in spite of notice, opponent no.1 owner of the Tanker did not contest, matter proceeded ex-parte against him.

Present appellant/original opponent no.2/Insurance Company resisted the claim petition by filing written statement vide exh.16 and in toto denied all the contentions raised in the claim petition except admission that Tanker was insured with them and also raising a plea of driver not holding effective driving licence.

3. In the light of above respective cases advanced, learned Tribunal reached to a finding that,
claimants proved that deceased Ganesh died due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tanker bearing no.MH45-4989 and therefore, consequently, held claimants to be entitled to receive compensation.
Finding was also recorded that present appellant failed to prove that there was breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy at the hands of original opponent no.1.

Learned Tribunal directed original opponent nos.1 and 2 to jointly and severally pay Rs.19,79,000/-
alongwith interest @ 8% p.a. vide its judgment and award dated 21-12-2016.

sentences.text: In the instant appeal, there is challenge to above judgment and award and primarily grounds raised are that, firstly there was no cogent, reliable, trustworthy evidence or pleadings about income of deceased and as such, there was no further question of awarding amount towards future prospects.
5. Learned counsel for original claimants justified and supported award passed by learned Tribunal and according to him, there is no error in the same so as to interfere.

6. Heard. Perused the record and the impugned judgment.
Admittedly, here, deceased was an agriculturist and also dealing with milk business.

On the basis of documentary evidence i.e. 7/12 extract of the agricultural land, which shows that deceased was taking cash crops like sugarcane, onion, sweet lemon, the learned Tribunal has considered notional income of deceased as Rs.6,500/- per month.
Consequently, it cannot be said that there was no evidence at all on the point of income of deceased.
The learned Tribunal, further by stating that deceased was 32 years old, added 50% amount of income towards future prospects.

As per decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others (2017) 16 SCC 680, in the cases where the deceased was self- employed and below 40 years of age, an addition of 40% of the income needs to be considered towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, in the present case, the learned Tribunal has apparently erred in considering 50%
amount of income towards future prospects because the deceased was self-employed and his age was 32 years at the time of incident, hence, 40% amount of income needs to be considered towards future prospects.

Accordingly, the calculation of compensation would be as under :
Sr. Particulars Amount No. (Rs.) (Rs.)
 1 Monthly Income = 6,500 Addition of 40% towards future prospects = 2,600 Total Monthly Income = 9,100 Annual Income (9,100 x 12) = 1,09,200 1,09,200 2
Less 1/4th deduction towards personal expenses 81,900 (1,09,200 - 27,300) = 81,900 3 Amount after considering Multiplier of 16 (81,900 x 16) 13,10,400
4 Non-pecuniary Losses : 5,75,000 Total Amount granted towards consortium, funeral expenses, loss of estate (as awarded by the Tribunal) 5
Total Compensation as per this Court 18,85,400 6 Amount of compensation granted by the Tribunal 19,79,000 7
Total Compensation as per this Court 18,85,400 8
Difference amount 93,600 {6} FA 1363 OF 2017 7.
In view of above discussion, the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.18,85,400/-.

Accordingly, following order is passed :
ORDER (i) First Appeal is partly allowed.

(ii) Impugned judgment and award dated 21-12-2016 passed by the Chairman,
MACT, Ahmednagar in MACP No. 245 of 2015 stands modified.
(iii) The claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.18,85,400/- along with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of realization of the amount.
(iv) Registry is directed to pay Rs.18,85,400/- to the claimants with accrued interest thereon till the date of its realization, out of the amount deposited by the appellant/Insurance Company.
Rest of the amount be refunded to the appellant/Insurance Company with accrued interest thereon.
(iv) Rest of the award passed by the Chairman, MACT, Ahmednagar is kept intact.
(v) Modified award be prepared accordingly.
(vi) The Appeal is disposed of in above terms.
